title: An optimized protocol to detect ubiquitination modification of exogenous or endogenous proteins
protocol: Observe the density of 293T cells under a microscope.
Discard the culture medium and change to 5 mL DMEM (No FBS, No antibiotics).
Mix an appropriate amount of plasmids with 250 μL DMEM (No FBS, No antibiotics) to prepare the DNA solution.
Add Lipofectamine 2000 reagent in a ratio of 1 μL: 1 μg plasmid in 250 μL DMEM (No FBS, No antibiotics).
Mix the diluted DNA solution dropwise with the diluted Lipofectamine 2000 solution while pipetting.
Incubate the DNA-Lipofectamine 2000 mixture at 25°C for 15 min.
Add the DNA-Lipofectamine 2000 mixture to the cells in a dropwise manner, gently swirling the plate.
Change to complete culture medium 4–6 h after transfection.
Incubate the cells in a 37°C incubator for 24 h to allow for protein expression.
Add MG132 to the 293T cells at a final concentration of 10 μM.
Incubate the cells in a 37°C incubator for 3–6 h.
Wash the cells with 3 mL PBS.
Discard PBS and add 700 μL cell lysis buffer (WB-IP) containing PMSF (100 nM) and protease inhibitor cocktail (100×).
Gently scrape the cells into a 1.5 mL EP tube and incubate on ice for 30 min.
Centrifuge the sample at 4°C and 14,000 × g for 5 min.
Separate the supernatant into a new EP tube.
Absorb 100 μL of supernatant as INPUT to detect the expression of transfected plasmids.
Add 25 μL 5 × loading buffer and boil the sample for 10 min at 100°C.
Store the sample at -20°C for up to 1 year if needed.
Add 3–5 μL of antibody specific to your target protein into the remanent supernatant.
Incubate and shake the mixture gently at 4°C for 1 h.
Add 40 μL of protein G beads that bind to the antibody to the mixture.
Incubate and shake the mixture gently at 4°C for 12–16 h.
Collect beads by centrifugation at 4°C and 14,000 × g for 30 seconds.
Absorb and discard supernatant with a pipette.
Wash beads with 1 mL PBS containing 25% lysis buffer WB-IP and 1% PMSF.
Shake mixture gently at 4°C for 10 minutes.
Repeat washing steps three times.
Collect beads by centrifugation at 4°C and 14,000 × g for 30 seconds.
Discard supernatant with a pipette.
Add 20 μL washing buffer to the beads.
Add 5 μL 5× loading buffer to the beads.
Boil mixture for 5 minutes at 100°C.
Prepare SDS-PAGE gels according to timing instructions.
Mix appropriate amounts of resolving gel solution as per formula.
Pour resolving gel solution into gel cassette, leaving 2 cm for stacking gel.
Add 1 mL ddH2O to the resolving gel solution.
Wait for approximately 30 minutes until a clear dividing line between water and gel is observed.
Mix appropriate amounts of stacking gel solution.
Pour the stacking gel solution on top of the resolving gel.
Insert the comb into the stacking gel solution.
Let the stacking gel polymerize for approximately 30 minutes.
Clamp the gel into the electrophoresis apparatus.
Fill the electrophoresis chambers with 1× SDS buffer.
Remove the comb and carefully load IP samples (20 μL) into the wells.
Load INPUT samples (20 μL) into the wells.
Load protein marker (5 μL) into the wells.
Run electrophoresis at 80 V until proteins run out of the stacking gel.
Change to 120 V and continue running until the dye front reaches the bottom of the gel.
Wet four pieces of filter paper with transmembrane buffer.
Place wet filter papers onto the transfer apparatus sequentially.
Soak a piece of PVDF membrane (6 cm × 9 cm) in methanol for 1 minute.
Place the PVDF membrane on top of the filter papers.
Wet the PVDF membrane with transmembrane buffer.
Carefully remove the gel from the cassette and rinse briefly with distilled water.
Place the gel onto the PVDF membrane, ensuring no air bubbles are present between them.
Wet four pieces of filter paper with transmembrane buffer.
Place wet filter papers onto the gel sequentially.
Clamp the transfer apparatus.
Add enough transmembrane buffer to the transfer apparatus to cover the gel and the membrane.
Run the transfer apparatus at 300 mA for the appropriate amount of time, depending on protein size and transfer efficiency.
Block the PVDF membrane with a blocking buffer (5% non-fat dry milk in TBST) for 2 h at 25°C.
Incubate the membrane with the primary antibody diluted in blocking buffer for 12–16 h at 4°C with gentle agitation.
Wash the membrane with TBST buffer three times for 10 min each to remove unbound primary antibody.
Incubate the membrane with the appropriate secondary antibody conjugated to horseradish peroxidase (HRP), diluted in blocking buffer, for 1 h at 25°C with gentle agitation.
Wash the membrane with TBST buffer three times for 10 min each to remove unbound secondary antibody.
Detect the protein using a chemiluminescence imaging system.
